definition.availability_rule: Use only observed closes at or before signal close t. Current historical download is not a vintage archive.
definition.execution_rule: No earlier than next observed close after t; last-row signal has no execution observation. No tradability or performance claim.
definition.hypothesis: Model hypothesis appears separately below; it is not a computed result.
definition.input_units: Unadjusted close in CNY/share; simple returns and final score dimensionless.
definition.name: Trailing close-return research candidate
definition.signal_rule: Signal after close t; require 6 trailing observations, positive volatility when normalized. No extra return-magnitude eligibility exclusion.
definition.universe: 601318.XSHG, 600036.XSHG, 300750.XSHE; fixed convenience sample, not a point-in-time universe.

limits: Development sample only; this inspected data cannot become an untouched holdout.
An available next observed close does not establish tradability, fills or transaction costs.

citations.quote: Normalization divides the trailing return by trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(lookback); this does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk.

decisions.reason: Accepted: eligibility is warmup-only and identical across symbols; close coverage is not tradability, and the sample is development-only, never a holdout.
Accepted: all inputs at or before the signal close, no filling of the observed union, execution no earlier than the next observed close, no corporate-action inference from jumps.
Accepted: raw scores keep each symbol's own return scale; recorded as a limitation of the retained baseline, motivating inspection of the alternative without any superiority claim.
Inspected and deferred: source-defined and coverage-equivalent, but the rendered comparison does not support the motivating comparability benefit, so adoption awaits the separate future evaluation.

hypothesis.text: Retained exploratory hypothesis: short-horizon close momentum measured as the trailing raw close-to-close return over the starting window with a positive sign, kept as the candidate for later independent evaluation; usefulness and the winning sign remain unproven. Source-supported applicability constraints: only observed unadjusted closes at or before the signal close enter a signal; the observed union is not an exchange calendar and windows are not filled; execution is no earlier than the next observed close after the signal, and an available next observed close is coverage rather than tradability; the universe is a small fixed convenience sample and not a holdout; close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions, so possible contamination is disclosed rather than handled by a return bound. A single motivated alternative, the source-defined realized-volatility normalization of the same trailing return, was inspected with an identical eligible cohort and is deferred rather than adopted; its observed score-scale change is not evidence of improvement.

rationale.text: Retention reasons: the coverage, timing and units findings are adopted as binding constraints, and the normalization hypothesis is inspected but deferred. The alternative was examined before deciding: it follows the source definition exactly, its eligible cohort and warmup treatment match the baseline, and its required treatment of non-positive trailing volatility, motivated by the recorded zero single-observation return for one symbol, is defined with consequences referenced through inspection facts rather than restated. The host-rendered scale-free comparison of cross-symbol score dispersion gives no support for the motivating comparability benefit, and the contract requires added parameters to be justified from cited evidence, so adopting the extra volatility window now would force an unsupported change; the raw-return baseline stays, with its documented limitation that scores inherit each symbol's own volatility scale. No daily-return bound is added because no cited evidence supports any cutoff and close-only jumps cannot be attributed to corporate actions. Observed scale changes are descriptive only: nothing establishes alpha, superiority, tradability or removal of systematic risk, and the normalized variant must never be called an annual Sharpe ratio.
